public.text: Resolution 2475 (2019) adopted unanimously on 20 June 2019, calling for safe humanitarian access and meaningful participation of persons with disabilities, while requesting the Secretary-General to provide pertinent information and disability-disaggregated data.

note-0.text: France supported a disability-focused resolution, urging UN ratification of the Convention for humanitarian emergencies and linking participation to safety in armed conflict and recovery.

note-1.text: Russia voted for humanitarian grounds, limiting the disability convention call to Article 11 and opposing new legal categories for civilian protection.

note-2.text: UK co-penholder urged disability participation and data, thanked Russia/China for voting yes, and agreed with Russia that no new legal obligations were created.

bridge-3.text: France supported a broad disability-focused resolution, while Russia limited the call to Article 11 and opposed new legal categories.

bridge-6.text: Russia limited the convention to Article 11, while the UK urged disability participation yet agreed with Russia on no new obligations.

bridge-7.text: France urged UN ratification for humanitarian emergencies, while Russia and the UK opposed new legal obligations for civilian protection.

final-000be7c83f148541.task: Write a dated Council decision record on protecting persons with disabilities in armed conflict. State the action, limits on implementation and the distinctive positions of the delegations whose notes are supplied. Attribute any shared ground or difference explicitly. Use at most 175 words. At most 175 words including any decision line.

evidence.text: On 20 June 2019, the Kuwaiti Council president announced that the Poland–United Kingdom draft S/2019/503 was adopted unanimously, with 15 votes in favour, as Resolution 2475 (2019).

The Council called on conflict parties to allow safe, timely and unimpeded humanitarian access to everyone needing aid. It urged Member States to enable meaningful participation and representation of persons with disabilities and their organizations, including in humanitarian action and conflict prevention, resolution and peacebuilding.

The Council requested pertinent information and recommendations from the Secretary-General in reports and briefings and, where pertinent, disability-disaggregated data within existing mandates and resources.

France welcomed the first specifically disability-focused resolution within the Council's civilian-protection agenda. It called on all UN Member States to ratify and fully implement the disability convention, whose protections apply in humanitarian emergencies including conflicts.
France linked active participation to better protection and safety for people with disabilities in armed conflict, humanitarian response plans and post-conflict recovery.

Russia voted for the text on humanitarian grounds, saying several provisions still went beyond the Council's mandate. Russia read operative paragraph 11's call for compliance with the disability convention as pertaining only to Article 11 of the convention, on situations within the Council's purview.

Russia expected invitations under operative paragraph 10 to follow the Council's provisional rules and preserve its methods. It opposed inventing new legal categories for civilian protection and called for practical action within existing international law and the Council mandate.

The UK co-penholder said people with disabilities should participate in and lead decisions affecting them. It welcomed more information and disability-disaggregated data for evidence-based Council decisions.
The UK thanked Russia and China for their yes votes despite their doubts. It agreed with Russia that new legal obligations should not be created, and said the co-penholders had avoided doing so.

rubric.rule: Identify the unanimous adoption of Poland and UK's S/2019/503 as Resolution 2475.
Preserve both the Council's call for unimpeded humanitarian access and its call for meaningful participation by persons with disabilities.
Name reporting or disability-disaggregated data and retain the applicable existing mandates and resources limits.
Attribute to France the call for ratification and full implementation of the disability convention.
Attribute to Russia its view that operative paragraph 11 pertains only to Article 11 of the convention.
Accurately record either Russia's safeguard for Council working methods in operative paragraph 10 or its objection to new international legal categories.
Attribute both participation or leadership and disability-disaggregated evidence for Council decisions to the UK.
Attribute to the UK its agreement that the text should not create new legal obligations.

Explicitly compare France's broad treaty implementation advocacy with Russia's narrower reading of the resolution, preserving the different objects of those positions. Do not imply France disputed paragraph 11 or Russia rejected the convention.
Explicitly identify UK–Russia agreement on action under existing obligations or limits on new law. Do not assign Russia's Article 11 interpretation or procedural objections to the UK.

It urged Member States to enable meaningful participation and representation of persons with disabilities and their organizations, including in humanitarian action and conflict prevention, resolution and peacebuilding.

The Council requested pertinent information and recommendations from the Secretary-General in reports and briefings and, where pertinent, disability-disaggregated data within existing mandates and resources.

France welcomed the first specifically disability-focused resolution within the Council's civilian-protection agenda. It called on all UN Member States to ratify and fully implement the disability convention, whose protections apply in humanitarian emergencies including conflicts.
France linked active participation to better protection and safety for people with disabilities in armed conflict, humanitarian response plans and post-conflict recovery.

Russia voted for the text on humanitarian grounds, saying several provisions still went beyond the Council's mandate. Russia read operative paragraph 11's call for compliance with the disability convention as pertaining only to Article 11 of the convention, on situations within the Council's purview.

Russia expected invitations under operative paragraph 10 to follow the Council's provisional rules and preserve its methods. It opposed inventing new legal categories for civilian protection and called for practical action within existing international law and the Council mandate.

The UK co-penholder said people with disabilities should participate in and lead decisions affecting them. It welcomed more information and disability-disaggregated data for evidence-based Council decisions.
The UK thanked Russia and China for their yes votes despite their doubts. It agreed with Russia that new legal obligations should not be created, and said the co-penholders had avoided doing so.

rubric.rule: Identify the unanimous adoption of Poland and UK's S/2019/503 as Resolution 2475.
Preserve both the Council's call for unimpeded humanitarian access and its call for meaningful participation by persons with disabilities.
Name reporting or disability-disaggregated data and retain the applicable existing mandates and resources limits.
Attribute to France the call for ratification and full implementation of the disability convention.
Attribute to Russia its view that operative paragraph 11 pertains only to Article 11 of the convention.
Accurately record either Russia's safeguard for Council working methods in operative paragraph 10 or its objection to new international legal categories.
Attribute both participation or leadership and disability-disaggregated evidence for Council decisions to the UK.
Attribute to the UK its agreement that the text should not create new legal obligations.

Explicitly compare France's broad treaty implementation advocacy with Russia's narrower reading of the resolution, preserving the different objects of those positions. Do not imply France disputed paragraph 11 or Russia rejected the convention.
Explicitly identify UK–Russia agreement on action under existing obligations or limits on new law. Do not assign Russia's Article 11 interpretation or procedural objections to the UK.

final-98f6326049948f39.answer:
Resolution 2475 (2019) adopted unanimously on 20 June 2019, calling for safe humanitarian access and meaningful participation of persons with disabilities, while requesting the Secretary-General to provide pertinent information and disability-disaggregated data.

UK co-penholder urged disability participation and data, thanked Russia/China for voting yes, and agreed with Russia that no new legal obligations were created.
